_: ccwire.v1.Frame ROUTING-HEADER vectors. Asserted by lib/ccwire/codecParity.selftest.ts
and services/transport/rust/tests/codec.rs.
HAND-WRITTEN from the protobuf wire specification, NOT dumped from either
implementation. A fixture generated by the code it checks only proves the code
agrees with itself. Tag byte = field*8 + wire_type; every expectation below was
computed from that rule by hand.
SCOPE - TWO SECTIONS, BECAUSE THERE ARE TWO LAYERS:
'decode'/'encode' are ROUTING-HEADER vectors. Both sides read the header the same
way and treat the body as opaque bytes there: codec.ts's decodeFrameMessage and
the Rust parse.rs both route on the field number without interpreting what is
inside. So every body in those two sections is empty or an UNTYPED field number.
'bodies' are BODY vectors, for the six types that ARE typed: submit_message 48
(with its nested Envelope and PublicMeta), typing_state 81, viewer_state 82,
geo_relay 84, crypto_control 98, fragment 112. Each entry is the body's own bytes.
The Rust side decodes them with services/transport/rust/src/body.rs; the
TypeScript side has no body-only entry point, so codecParity.selftest.ts wraps
each one in the smallest legal frame (traffic_class CONTROL plus the body's tag)
and reads the result out of Frame.value. Both therefore decode the body at nesting
depth 1, which is what the frame layer already charged for entering it.
'value' is the decoded message with proto3 defaults materialised, exactly as
codec.ts surfaces them: bytes fields as hex, 64-bit fields as DECIMAL STRINGS (a
double rounds 2^53+1 away; Rust uses native u64/i64 and the test parses the
string, so both agree on the VALUE), unknown enum values retained as their number
and surfaced as *_UNSPECIFIED, and unknown fields preserved verbatim, tag included.
THERE IS NO LONGER A BODY TYPE ONLY ONE SIDE DECODES. Until body.rs existed, a
MALFORMED body of one of those six was refused by codec.ts and accepted by Rust,
which never looked inside. The malformed and over-bound cases now live below and
both sides must refuse them for the SAME typed reason, so
bodiesTypedByTypescriptOnly is empty. It stays as an asserted (now vacuous)
exclusion rather than being deleted: if a body is ever typed on one side only,
this is where that is recorded, and the assertion is what stops the gap from
reopening silently.
The Go implementation is the third reader of this file and, like the Rust one
before body.rs, it routes without decoding bodies. It asserts the header sections
and ignores 'bodies' - a section a decoder does not implement is not a vector it
can fail. Adding typed bodies in Go means reading 'bodies' the way
services/transport/rust/tests/body.rs does; the vectors are already here.

bodies.name: typing_state canonical
bodies.why: f1w2 tag 0x0a len 2 'c1'; f2w0 tag 0x10 value 1; f3w2 tag 0x1a len 2 'u9'.

bodies.name: typing_state empty - proto3 defaults are materialised
bodies.why: A zero-byte body is a legal message. Absent string is '', absent bool false.

bodies.name: typing_state keeps a known field with the WRONG wire type as unknown
bodies.why: 0801 is field 1 (chat_id) as a VARINT, not length-delimited. codec.ts matches on (field, wire) together, so this is an unknown field, not an error. 2807 is field 5, which does not exist. Both are preserved verbatim, tag included.

bodies.name: typing_state duplicate scalar is last-wins
bodies.why: proto3's rule. typing=true then typing=false leaves false.

bodies.name: typing_state chat_id that is not UTF-8 is refused
bodies.why: 0xff 0xfe is not valid UTF-8. Refused, never replaced with U+FFFD - substituting would make the two sides disagree about what the bytes said.

bodies.name: typing_state chat_id over the negotiated string bound is refused
bodies.why: max_string_field_bytes tightened to 4; a 5-byte chat_id is refused on the BYTE length, before any UTF-8 decode.

bodies.name: typing_state with a length running past the end is refused
bodies.why: chat_id declares 5 bytes, 2 follow. THE MALFORMED CASE the Rust side used to accept because it never looked inside a body.

bodies.name: typing_state with an over-long length varint is refused
bodies.why: Five continuation bytes in LENGTH position. A varint longer than five bytes there is not a large number, it is an over-long encoding probing for a parser mismatch.

bodies.name: typing_state with a proto2 group is refused
bodies.why: 0x0b = field 1, wire type 3. Groups are not representable in proto3 and are refused rather than skipped.

bodies.name: viewer_state canonical
bodies.why: chat_id 'c1'; activity 2 = VIEWER_ACTIVITY_TYPING (f2w0 0x10); resync true (f4w0 0x20). leaving is absent, so false.

bodies.name: viewer_state retains an enum value this build does not know
bodies.why: 99 = 0x63. envelope.proto's decoder contract: the NUMBER is authoritative and re-encodes; the name surfaces as *_UNSPECIFIED so application code cannot branch on a meaning it does not have.

bodies.name: viewer_state empty
bodies.why: activity 0 surfaces as VIEWER_ACTIVITY_UNSPECIFIED, which is a real value here and not an error.

bodies.name: viewer_state field number 0 is refused
bodies.why: Tag 0x00 is field 0, which is not a representable proto field number, so its presence is not a mistake.

bodies.name: viewer_state with a truncated varint is refused
bodies.why: Tag says field 2, wire 0, and the body ends. A varint scan must not walk off the buffer.

bodies.name: geo_relay canonical
bodies.why: scope_kind 1 = SCOPE_KIND_CHAT; scope_id 'g'; subject_id 's'; sealed aabb; until_ms 300 = varint ac 02 (300 = 2*128 + 44); sender_uid 'u'.

bodies.name: geo_relay until_ms is a SIGNED int64
bodies.why: ff*9 then 01 is all 64 bits set. As int64 that is -1, not 18446744073709551615. Reading this field unsigned would put an expiry 584 million years in the future on a share that has already ended.

bodies.name: geo_relay empty
bodies.why: Every default materialised, including the 64-bit one as '0'.

bodies.name: geo_relay sealed over max_opaque_bytes is refused
bodies.why: max_opaque_bytes tightened to 4; sealed declares 5. sealed is routed and never read, which is exactly why its size is bounded rather than trusted.

bodies.name: crypto_control canonical
bodies.why: kind 2 = MEDIA_KEY; chat_id 'c'; to_uid 'u'; payload aabb; epoch 2^53+1 = 81 80 80 80 80 80 80 10 (1 at shift 0, 16 at shift 49 = 2^53); payload_format 'v1'.

bodies.name: crypto_control epoch = u64 max
bodies.why: epoch is UNSIGNED, unlike geo_relay.until_ms with the identical bytes. The two must not be read the same way.

bodies.name: crypto_control empty
bodies.why: A key event with nothing in it is still a well-formed message; refusing it is the application's call, not the codec's.

bodies.name: crypto_control with a varint that never terminates is refused
bodies.why: Ten continuation bytes in VALUE position. Sixty-four bits cannot need an eleventh byte.

bodies.name: submit_message canonical, nested two deep
bodies.why: SubmitMessage{envelope(23 bytes), sealed aabb}. Envelope{chat_id 'c', server_ts_ms 1000 = varint e8 07, msg_class 1 = NORMAL, public_meta(13 bytes)}. PublicMeta{attachment_id 'a', view_once true, option_count 3, mention_user_ids ['x','y']}. Lengths: PublicMeta 3+2+2+3+3 = 13 = 0x0d; Envelope 3+3+2+(2+13) = 23 = 0x17.

bodies.name: submit_message with no envelope leaves it ABSENT, not defaulted
bodies.why: Submessage presence is meaningful in proto3: an absent Envelope and an all-default one are different frames and must not be collapsed into each other.

bodies.name: submit_message empty
bodies.why: No envelope, no sealed.

bodies.name: submit_message entering the envelope costs depth
bodies.why: max_nesting_depth tightened to 1. The body itself sits at depth 1 - the frame layer already charged for entering it - so the envelope at depth 2 is over the limit. Checked BEFORE its declared length is read.

bodies.name: submit_message sealed over max_message_body_bytes is refused
bodies.why: sealed is the ONE field bounded at max_message_body_bytes rather than max_opaque_bytes - it arrives reassembled from fragments, so it legitimately exceeds a single frame. Tightened to 4; sealed declares 5.

bodies.name: submit_message mention_user_ids over max_repeated_elements is refused
bodies.why: max_repeated_elements tightened to 2, three mentions inside PublicMeta. Checked BEFORE the third element is appended, so a repeated field cannot grow the heap past the cap even by one. Lengths: PublicMeta 9 = 0x09, Envelope 2+9 = 11 = 0x0b.

bodies.name: submit_message with a truncated envelope is refused
bodies.why: The envelope declares 5 bytes and 2 follow. A nested declared length must never size an allocation either.

bodies.name: fragment canonical
bodies.why: fragment_id 'f1'; index 1; total 3; total_bytes 9; chunk aabbcc; last absent so false.

bodies.name: fragment empty
bodies.why: Defaults, with total_bytes as '0'.

bodies.name: fragment total over max_fragments_per_message is refused
bodies.why: 17 = 0x11, against the default ceiling of 16. No tightened limits: this one is over the bound this build ships with.

bodies.name: fragment total_bytes over max_message_body_bytes is refused
bodies.why: 1048577 = 2^20 + 1 = varint 81 80 40, one over the default 1 MiB. Declared up front and checked BEFORE anything is allocated from it - the reassembler must not be handed a number it would trust.

bodies.name: fragment with a truncated chunk is refused
bodies.why: chunk declares 5 bytes and 2 follow. chunk carries no bound of its own - it is bounded by the frame - so the truncation check is the only thing standing here.

decode.name: minimal valid frame - traffic_class CONTROL and nothing else
decode.why: tag 0x10 = field 2 (traffic_class), wire 0. Value 1 = TRAFFIC_CLASS_CONTROL.

decode.name: every routing field set
decode.why: 0a03 616263 = field 1 len 3 'abc'; 1002 tc; 1802 stream; 2007 seq=7.

decode.name: seq = 2^53+1, the value a JS number silently rounds away
decode.why: envelope.proto marks seq JS_STRING for exactly this. 2^53+1 varint-encodes as 81 80 80 80 80 80 80 10: 1 at shift 0, then 16 at shift 49 = 2^53. If either side reads this through a double it comes back as 9007199254740992 and a replay window opens itself.

decode.name: seq = u64 max
decode.why: ff*9 then 01: 63 one-bits then bit 63.

decode.name: depends_on carries the causal epoch
decode.why: tag 0x28 = field 5, wire 0.

decode.name: EPHEMERAL carrying typing_state is allowed
decode.why: field 81 wire 2 = 81*8+2 = 650 = varint 8a 05. Empty body, length 00.

decode.name: an empty body is still a body
decode.why: field 19 (ping) wire 2 = 154 = varint 9a 01, length 00. A bare Ping is a zero-byte submessage; bodyField must still be set or the frame loses its meaning.

decode.name: an untyped body round-trips verbatim
decode.why: field 22 (ack) wire 2 = 178 = varint b2 01, length 3. Contents are not parsed by either side, so the bytes must survive exactly.

decode.name: an unknown field is preserved, never dropped
decode.why: field 7 wire 0 = 0x38, value 42 = 0x2a. envelope.proto requires unknown fields be PRESERVED; the tag+value bytes are kept verbatim so a re-encode is byte-identical.

decode.name: a duplicate scalar is last-wins
decode.why: proto3's rule. Both sides must apply it; deviating is how a parser differential is born.

decode.name: traffic_class UNSPECIFIED is refused
decode.why: envelope.proto: TRAFFIC_CLASS_UNSPECIFIED is 'never valid on the wire; refuse'. An empty buffer decodes to it.

decode.name: EPHEMERAL carrying crypto_control is a protocol violation
decode.why: THE INVARIANT. field 98 wire 2 = 786 = varint 92 06. A key event must not inherit droppable, datagram-eligible scheduling - envelope.proto says refuse, 'never handled leniently'.

decode.name: EPHEMERAL carrying device_event is a protocol violation
decode.why: Same invariant, an untyped body: it is enforced on the field number, so it holds for all 27 bodies. field 97 wire 2 = 778 = varint 8a 06.

decode.name: two bodies in one frame are refused
decode.why: A oneof is ONE field. proto3 says last-wins; both implementations refuse instead, because if one side took the last and another took the first they would disagree about what the peer said while both called it valid.

decode.name: field number 0 is refused
decode.why: Not a representable proto field number, so its presence is not a mistake.

decode.name: wire type 3 (proto2 group) is refused
decode.why: field 9 wire 3 = 75 = 0x4b. Groups are not representable in proto3 and are a classic parser-differential vector, so they are refused rather than skipped.

decode.name: wire type 4 (group end) is refused
decode.why: field 9 wire 4 = 76 = 0x4c.

decode.name: a length running past the end is refused, not allocated
decode.why: field 1 declares 5 bytes; 2 follow. THE CHECK THIS LAYER EXISTS FOR - the declared length must never size an allocation.

decode.name: a varint that never terminates is refused
decode.why: Ten continuation bytes. Without this bound a varint scan walks off the buffer.

decode.name: an over-long TAG varint is refused at the frame layer
decode.why: 8a 80 80 80 80 00 is six bytes encoding the value 0x0a - tag for field 1, wire 2 - padded with redundant continuation bytes. A varint in TAG position is capped at FIVE bytes: a longer one is not a large number, it is an over-long encoding probing for a mismatch. Read as a full 64-bit varint instead, this decodes to field 1 wire 2 and then runs out of input, refusing the SAME BYTES for a DIFFERENT reason (TRUNCATED). That divergence was real: parse.rs read ten bytes here until this vector pinned it.

decode.name: an over-long LENGTH varint is refused at the frame layer
decode.why: traffic_class CONTROL, then request_id (0a) whose length 1 is written as 81 80 80 80 80 00 - six bytes - followed by 'a'. Read as a full 64-bit varint this is an ACCEPTED frame with request_id 'a'; capped at five bytes it is refused. Accept-vs-refuse on identical bytes is the worst class of parser differential, so the cap is the contract and this vector is where all three meet.

decode.name: a truncated varint is refused
decode.why: A continuation bit with nothing after it.

decode.name: a request_id that is not UTF-8 is refused
decode.why: 0xff 0xfe is not valid UTF-8. Checked AFTER the length bound, so an oversized string is refused before any decode is attempted.

decode.name: a request_id over the negotiated string bound is refused
decode.why: With max_string_field_bytes tightened to 4, a 5-byte request_id is refused - and refused on the BYTE length, before UTF-8 decoding.

decode.name: a payload over the negotiated frame size is refused first
decode.why: maxBytes 2, buffer 4. Checked before anything is parsed, so every bound below it bounds something already known to be small.

decode.name: too many unknown fields are refused
decode.why: With max_repeated_elements tightened to 2, a third unknown field is refused. Unknown fields are preserved, but preservation is not unbounded.

decode.name: a frame already past the recursion limit is refused
decode.why: depth 7 > max_nesting_depth 6. The fragment reassembler passes depth+1 when it re-decodes a reassembled payload; this is what stops a Fragment-in-Fragment bomb.

decode.name: entering a body costs depth
decode.why: At depth 6 the frame itself is fine, but the body is a nested message, so depth+1 = 7 exceeds the limit. The charge applies even though neither side parses this body.

encode.name: proto3 defaults are not written
encode.why: Only traffic_class is non-default, so only its tag and value appear.

encode.name: field order is 1,2,3,4,5 then body then unknown
encode.why: Order is part of the contract, not an implementation detail: it is what makes decode-then-encode byte-identical across both languages.

encode.name: a 2^53+1 sequence survives the round trip
encode.why: The value that a double would round away.

encode.name: an empty body is written anyway
encode.why: Unlike every other field. Dropping it would erase which body was set, turning a bare Ping into a frame with no meaning.

encode.name: unknown fields are written back verbatim, after the body
encode.why: Preservation is only real if it survives the re-encode.

encode.name: encode refuses the EPHEMERAL invariant too
encode.why: envelope.proto: 'enforced at both encode and decode'. A bug that produces this should fail on the machine that has the stack trace, not on the peer that only has bytes.

encode.name: encode refuses an unset traffic class
encode.why: Never valid on the wire, in either direction.
